questions.question: What is an inside rearview mirror used for?

options.text: Look at the outside of the bus.

questions.explanation: On a school bus, the inside rearview mirror is used to watch what passengers are doing. It should be adjusted so you can see every student on the bus, including those directly behind you.

questions.question: At stops, a driver should:

options.text: Tell passengers about dangers as they leave.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell passengers about dangers as they leave.
questions.explanation: At bus stops, tell passengers about possible dangers. For example, warn them to watch their step when getting off the bus.

questions.question: When a bus stops at an intermediate stop or final destination, passengers should be told:
questions.explanation: When stopping the bus at an intermediate stop or final destination, announce the stop location. You should also tell passengers the reason for the stop, when the bus will leave next, and the bus number.

questions.question: During a trip, carry-on baggage should:

options.text: Be stored away from the aisle.
Be kept on the rider's lap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be stored away from the aisle.
questions.explanation: Keep aisles and stairwells clear at all times. This prevents passengers from tripping.

questions.question: What kind of brakes do most new heavy-duty trucks use?
questions.explanation: Most new heavy-duty vehicles use dual air brake systems. This system has two separate air brake systems that use one set of brake controls.

questions.question: For a triple combination vehicle with air brakes, the leakage rate should be no more than ____ in one minute during a static leakage test.
questions.explanation: During a static leakage test on a triple combination vehicle with air brakes, air should leak no more than 5 psi in one minute. If air leaks faster than this, something needs repair and the vehicle should not be driven.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system:

options.text: Air tanks are shared between both systems.
Each system has its own air tanks.
You must choose which system to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own air tanks.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems. Both systems share one set of brake controls, but each system has its own tanks, hoses, and lines.

questions.question: When parallel parking, you should:

options.text: Back up past the space, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
Pull forward directly into the space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: For parallel parking, drive past the space first. Then back your vehicle into it, keeping the rear as close as possible to the back of the space. Your vehicle must fit completely within the space boundaries.

questions.question: Air tank drains should:

options.text: Not be used by the driver.
Only be used when it rains.
Be used to empty the tanks completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be used to empty the tanks completely.
questions.explanation: Compressed air in an air brake system usually contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up. Open the manual air tank drains daily to remove this buildup.

questions.question: What is brake lag?

options.text: The time between pressing the brake pedal and the brakes working
The distance between the brake pedal and the floor
The amount of air pressure needed to stop the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: The time between pressing the brake pedal and the brakes working
questions.explanation: Air takes time to travel through air lines to reach the brakes. So air brakes do not work right away. There is usually a delay of at least half a second between when you press the brake pedal and when the brakes start to work.

questions.question: When operating a school bus, when should mirrors be adjusted?
questions.explanation: Safe school bus operation depends on properly adjusted mirrors. Always check each mirror before you start driving.

questions.question: In a newer vehicle, how is the parking brake applied?

options.text: Moving a lever to the right.

questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, the parking brake is controlled by a yellow, diamond-shaped knob. Pull it outward to apply the brakes and push it inward to release them.

questions.question: What might you be asked to do during a basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: Drive straight into a parking space.

questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset backing, parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: If an air compressor is belt-driven, what should be checked about the belt?
questions.explanation: If your vehicle has air brakes, check the air compressor drive belt before each drive. Check that it is tight and in good condition.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi within how many seconds?
questions.explanation: When checking a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems within about 45 seconds.

questions.question: Before going down a hill, what gear should you switch into?
questions.explanation: Before going downhill, switch into a low gear. Gravity will speed up your vehicle as you go down.

questions.question: Which statement about school buses and ABS is correct?

options.text: School buses are never equipped with ABS.
School buses are only equipped with ABS in cold climates.
School buses may be equipped with ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: School buses may be equipped with ABS.
questions.explanation: Most commercial vehicles made after 1998 or 1999 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS). Many older buses also have ABS.

questions.question: Which item is not part of a vehicle's air brake system?
questions.explanation: Air brake systems include an air compressor, air storage tanks, gauges, warning devices, brakes, and controls. An air filter is not part of the air brake system.

questions.question: When arriving at a destination, what should a driver do?

options.text: Remind passengers to take their belongings when they exit.
Only make announcements after passengers start exiting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remind passengers to take their belongings when they exit.
questions.explanation: When arriving at a stop, remind passengers to take all belongings before exiting. It is best to make this announcement before the bus fully stops.

questions.question: Except for straight line backing, how many times may a driver exit their vehicle to check position during testing?
questions.explanation: A driver may exit the vehicle to check position during testing. For straight line backing, a driver may only check once. For all other exercises, a driver may check up to two times.
